description: We're CLEO, exploring AI, space, and Earth science through NASA's open data. We're looking for curious developers, designers, researchers, and innovators ready to collaborate, experiment, and build something meaningful at NASA Space Apps 2026 in Mangalore!
summary:
CLEO is a web-based fire activity intelligence platform designed to harmonize NASA's MODIS and VIIRS active-fire satellite observations into a unified historical burning-activity record.

The platform enables users to select geographical areas of interest and explore historical fire activity through interactive maps, temporal visualizations, and a burning-activity calendar. By bringing together observations from two different satellite sensor systems, CLEO aims to address inconsistencies in the way historical fire detections are analyzed and compared.

Users can investigate recurring seasonal patterns, examine changes in burning activity across different years, and identify unusual periods of elevated hotspot activity. The platform is designed to support researchers, environmental scientists, land managers, and emergency response teams in understanding historical fire patterns and improving monitoring preparedness.

CLEO transforms fragmented satellite observations into an accessible analytical experience, making historical fire intelligence easier to explore and interpret.
details:
Overview

CLEO is an interactive geospatial intelligence application developed to address the fragmentation of historical satellite-based active-fire observations. It brings together NASA's MODIS and VIIRS hotspot records within a unified analytical framework, allowing users to investigate burning activity across geographical regions and historical periods.

How It Works

The platform follows a structured data-processing and visualization workflow:

1. Data Acquisition

CLEO uses satellite-based active-fire observations from NASA's MODIS and VIIRS instruments. These records contain important information, including geographical coordinates, observation timestamps, sensor information, fire confidence, and Fire Radiative Power (where available).

2. Data Harmonization

Since MODIS and VIIRS have different spatial resolutions, observation characteristics, and temporal coverage, their raw detection counts cannot simply be treated as directly equivalent.

CLEO organizes observations into a common analytical structure to enable more consistent geographical and temporal comparisons.

[Add your actual sensor-normalization or calibration methodology here.]

3. Geographical Analysis

Users can select a specific Area of Interest (AOI) to investigate fire activity within a chosen geographical boundary and time period.

4. Burning Activity Calendar

Historical detections are organized into temporal visualizations, enabling users to examine monthly and yearly burning patterns, identify recurring periods of activity, and compare fire activity across different years.

5. Historical Pattern Analysis

The platform aims to make unusual burning conditions and historically significant periods easier to identify through comparisons with historical activity.

[Include anomaly detection or critical-period identification only if implemented.]

Intended Impact

CLEO aims to make more than two decades of satellite-based fire observations accessible through a single analytical interface.

Its intended applications include:

  • Helping emergency response teams understand historical fire activity.
  • Supporting land managers in identifying recurring fire seasons.
  • Enabling researchers to investigate long-term geographical and temporal fire patterns.
  • Supporting environmental monitoring and preparedness through accessible satellite-derived information.

Innovation

The central idea behind CLEO is not simply displaying satellite hotspots. It is making observations from different generations of Earth-observation instruments more usable together, providing users with a consistent starting point for exploring historical burning activity.
